text:
Single-negative BCE is a plausible bottleneck, but weak training margins do not establish the cause of Electronics validation performance. [gSASRec (IJCAI 2024)](https://www.ijcai.org/proceedings/2024/0939.pdf) directly studies SASRec’s negative-sampling overconfidence: increasing negatives and using generalized BCE improves effectiveness; authors recommend 128–256 negatives and correction parameter t=0.75 as practical defaults. This corrects sampling-induced overconfidence, rather than identifying false negatives. [Sampled-softmax research (2024)](https://wujcan.github.io/papers/tois-ssm.pdf) also highlights temperature sensitivity: overly hard negatives can dominate gradients, while in-batch sampling changes popularity pressure without guaranteeing better accuracy.

Recent work supports informative, diverse negatives with safeguards. [Negative Selection and Augmentation (2025)](https://ietresearch.onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1049/aie2.70004) combines batch/global negative selection with synthetic hard negatives for sequential contrastive learning. [EMM (2026)](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0893608026004090), broader contrastive-recommendation work, uses a refreshed memory bank and excludes positive/self IDs plus candidates outside a similarity window. These results motivate controlled hardness rather than selecting only the highest-scoring negatives; similarity filtering remains heuristic because unobserved items are not verified dislikes.

Practical experiment proposal: retain SASRec and compare baseline BCE against 128/256-negative gBCE and temperature-tuned sampled softmax. Exclude padding, target duplicates and known training positives; test a modest hard-negative mixture only after uniform sampling. Nonuniform sampled softmax should account for its sampling distribution. Use training histories alone for exclusions, with no future-label access. Select by the pinned four-category macro validation HR@10 and inspect category results; the cited studies do not establish improvement on this benchmark.
